To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic hypoxemia attenuates the alpha-1 adrenergic receptor-induced InsP3 formation in the uterino artery and that this attenuation is due to a reduction in coupling efficiency and InsP3 binding to InsP3-receptors.
chronic hypoxemia attenuates the ability of norepineprine to induce contraction and InsP3 production in the ovine uteroplacental circulation.
chronic hypoxemia attenuates alpha-1 adrenoreceptor-mediated InsP3 signaling in the ovine uterone artery by decreasing coupling efficiency and InsP3 receptor affinity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of chronic fetal hypoxia on the contractile response and the underlying signal transduction mechanism(s) in the uteroplacental vasculature.
the effect of chronic maternal hypoxia on vascular reactivity and signal transduction in the ovine uteroplacental circulation.
the effect of chronic maternal hypoxia on the vascular contractility and the underlying mechanism of action of the alpha-1 adrenergic agonist, phenylephrine, in the ovine uteroplacental circulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic hypoxemia reduces alpha-1 adrenergic receptor-mediated InsP3 signaling by decreasing the coupling efficiency and by decreasing InsP3 binding to its receptor.

chronic hypoxemia decreases alpha-1 adrenoreceptor-mediated inosital 1,4.5-trisphosphated (InsP3)-mediated contractile response in uterine artery by a combination of a decrease in the potency and efficacy of alpha-1 receptors to InsP3 signaling.

the alpha-1 adrenergic receptor-mediated contractile response of the uterinal artery to norepinephine is reduced in chronic hypoxia, due primarily to a decrease in coupling efficiency of alpha-adrenoceptors to Ins(1,4, 5) trisphosphate synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

chronic hypoxemia attenuates alpha-1 adrenergic vasoconstriction in the ovine uterinoartery, which is mediated by a reduction in coupling efficiency of alpha-adrenoceptors to Ins P3 synthesis and a decrease in contractile sensitivity to the second messenger Ins P3.

chronic hypoxemia attenuates the alpha-1 adrenergic response in the uterino-arterial vasculature, and the decreased responsiveness is mediated by a decrease in the coupling efficiency of alpha 1 adrenoceptors and InsP3 receptors, and a decrease in the sensitivity of the tissue contractile machinery to InsP3.

chronic hypoxemia attenuates alpha-1 adrenergic vasoconstriction in the uterino-placental vasculature by impairing the coupling efficiency of the receptor to InsP3 formation and by reducing the sensitivity of the InsP 3 receptors to the agonist.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hypoxia can alter vascular function by affecting the signaling pathways of the receptors.
chronic hypoxemia decreases the contractile sensitivity of ovine uterines to InsP3, which is a key mediator of vasoconstrictor-induced contractions.
chronic hypoxemia, which is a common feature of preeclampsia, impairs the contractile response of the uteroplacental vasculature to vasoconstrictor agonists.
